title: Tautological degree-one quotient charts, restriction and free comparisons
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal E$ an arbitrary quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and $p:P=\operatorname{Proj}_S A_S(\mathcal E)\to S$, where $A_S(\mathcal E)$ is the canonical symmetric graded algebra [def-trf-canonical-symmetric-graded-algebra] and relative Proj is [def-nagata-relative-proj]. No finite-type or local-freeness hypothesis is imposed on $\mathcal E$. There exists a normalized tautological quotient datum $D=(Q,q_P)$ [def-per-projective-bundle-quotient-data], with the following explicit chart and comparison properties. For every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$, set $M=\mathcal E(U)$ and $A=\operatorname{Sym}_R M$. For all $m\in M$ put $e=\iota(m)\in A_1$ and $H_e=(A_e)_0$ (degree-zero homogeneous localization [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]). The charts $C_e=D_+(e)=\operatorname{Spec}H_e$ cover $p^{-1}U$. On $C_e$, $Q$ identifies with the affine degree-one twist $(A_e)_1$ [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]; multiplication by $e$ gives an isomorphism $H_e\xrightarrow{\sim}(A_e)_1$ whose inverse sends $a/e^k$ to $a/e^{k+1}$. The quotient sends a pulled local section $v\in M$ to $\iota(v)/1$, with coefficient $\iota(v)/e$ in the frame $e$. In particular $q_P:p^*\mathcal E\twoheadrightarrow Q$ is surjective. For $f=\iota(n)$ the overlap is $D(f/e)\subset C_e$ and its frame transition is $e=(e/f)f$; the transitions satisfy the triple-overlap cocycle. Restriction on the base sends $a/e^k$ to $\bar a/\bar e^k$ and the frame $e$ to $\bar e$ on affine refinements, compatibly with these quotient maps. For every open $V\subseteq S$, the canonical identification $P\times_S V\simeq\operatorname{Proj}_V A_V(\mathcal E|_V)$ [def-pc-fibre-product] carries the restriction of $(Q,q_P)$ to its normalized twist and quotient. For $\mathcal E=\mathcal O_S^{\oplus(r+1)}$, $r\ge0$, the ordered basis gives an identification with relative projective space [def-nagata-relative-projective-space] carrying $Q$ to its standard twist [def-pc-projective-space-twist] and the basis quotient sections to $T_0,\ldots,T_r$. On an affine base $\operatorname{Spec}R$ this is the pair $(\operatorname{Proj}R[T_0,\ldots,T_r],\widetilde{R[T_0,\ldots,T_r](1)})$, with frames $T_i$ and transitions $T_i=(T_i/T_j)T_j$. All assertions include empty charts, the zero module and $r=0$.

proof.text: Use normalized quotient descent to obtain D and the chart-compatible affine restriction isomorphisms carrying every degree-one section to its restriction. The remaining degree-zero fraction equation is exactly HomogeneousLocalization.Away.map_mk. The identical isomorphism and its two normalization equations are packaged as NormalizedAffineRestriction, avoiding repeated expansion of the sheaf and colimit constructions in the kernel.
Apply the open-base comparison and ordered free comparison to this same normalized datum D. Both results hold for any D satisfying the original normalization.

For an affine U, the canonical degree-one inclusion lands in the grading by the range definition. The subalgebra generated by all iota(m) is the whole symmetric algebra, by symmetric-algebra induction; hence Proj.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top' proves that their basic opens cover. The standard opens are affine. Multiplication by e identifies degree zero and degree one by degreePart.powDivPowEquiv, and the twist free-generator API identifies those modules with the actual twist sections. This constructs phi and tau, with inverse, scalar action and pointwise fraction evaluation checked in ordinary localizations.

Evaluate unitToTwist and twistPowSection pointwise in the same prime localization to prove the quotient coefficient formula. The scalar f/e is a unit precisely where f is outside the prime, giving the scheme-basicOpen equality. The existing transition identity gives e=(e/f)f. Multiply the scalar cocycle by the free frame g and cancel using its free-generator injectivity; both sides reduce pointwise to the same unitToTwist section. Combine these affine formulas with the three preceding results by conjunction and existential introduction.
